title: Redwood POC weekly sync - Quantaco AI cost econ
summary: Week 4 sync: reviewed benchmark results for cost/unit and latency, discussed KV/prefix caching benefits, batching tradeoffs and suggested tunings. Agreed next steps to run 30-min throughput benchmark with updated batching and caching, Redwood to share revised cost spreadsheet and suggested quantization profiles.
next_steps: Alex to share updated cost model spreadsheet with per-route breakdown by 2026-09-24
Quantaco to run 30-minute peak throughput benchmark (SE-configured) by 2026-09-29
Priya to provide recommended batching + cache config and suggested quantization profiles by 2026-09-25
Schedule security follow-up re: KMS/SOC2 evidence with Jordan and Redwood security by 2026-10-01
action_items: Alex Chen - send updated cost spreadsheet with tokens/sec/$ calc by 2026-09-24
Priya Nair - share recommended batching configs and KV cache TTL suggestions by 2026-09-25
Samir Patel - run 30-min benchmark with instructed load and share logs by 2026-09-29
Jordan Reeves - gather KMS/KV network diagrams and data residency constraints by 2026-09-30
transcript:
[00:00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call?
[00:00:05] Samir Patel: Samir here.
[00:00:07] Maya Lopez: Maya here.
[00:00:09] Jordan Reeves: Jordan on infra.
[00:00:12] Priya Nair: Priya from Redwood, SE.
[00:00:15] Alex Chen: Cool. Agenda for today - quick run through of the cost/econ results from last week's run, talk tuning options (batching, cache, quant), and decide next benchmark.
[00:00:30] Maya Lopez: Sounds good. We pivoted priorities a bit, but cost is still top two.
[00:00:38] Alex Chen: Right. Priya, do you want to walk the numbers?
[00:00:42] Priya Nair: Yep. So we took your baseline trace and ran it across three configs: hosted small (g4-like), dedicated A100-40, and quantized A100 with int8-ish profile. We measured tokens per second per dollar and 95th p99 latency at 512 prefix. The headline: caching saves 30-45% token cost for repetitive prompts, and batching increases tokens/sec but can push tail latency up if you set large batching windows.
[00:01:12] Samir Patel: Wait, 30-45% from caching? That seems high. Is that for high prefix reuse only?
[00:01:18] Priya Nair: Good call - it's workload dependent. For the QnA route where 60% of calls hit a shared corp prefix, prefix/KV caching gave us ~40% token reduction overall. For pure chat sessions with long unique history it was lower, like 10-12%. The spreadsheet I sent has the per-route breakdown.
[00:01:34] Maya Lopez: Is that prefix cache the thing that stores KV of past tokens?
[00:01:38] Priya Nair: Yeah, KV cache / prefix caching - we store the activations for the shared prefixes to avoid recomputing the first N tokens. It reduces compute and effective tokens on the model. Note: network and cache TTLs matter for hosted vs vpc.
[00:01:50] Jordan Reeves: For our infra we'd prefer Dedicated because of data isolation, but cost delta is significant. How do tokens/sec/$ compare?
[00:01:58] Priya Nair: On dedicated A100-40 with moderate batching we saw ~2.8M tokens per dollar in the quant profile, hosted baseline was ~1.1M tokens/$, so about 2.5x improvement but depends on utilization. If you only run 20% utilization, unit economics shift back to hosted.
[00:02:15] Samir Patel: How are you calculating tokens per dollar? Is that tokens generated per $1 of infra over the run?
[00:02:20] Priya Nair: Yes - we amortize the GPU cost over the measured token output in the run and include per-request overhead (network + small infra). It's in the cost sheet column 'tokens_per_$'.
[00:02:27] Alex Chen: There's also model quality tradeoffs with quant. Priya, did we see any regen or hallucination differences?
[00:02:32] Priya Nair: Minimal at int8 for most of your prompts - we did a token-level eval with your golden set. Some long-context retrieval cases saw minor hallucination changes at int8 - so we recommended a hybrid: quantized for inference routes with short outputs and full precision for critical longform generation.
[00:02:48] Maya Lopez: That hybrid idea sounds promising. For product, short responses are most common.
[00:02:52] Jordan Reeves: Can you remind me about batching tradeoffs? We were seeing better throughput but p95 latency spikes.
[00:02:57] Priya Nair: Right - batching increases GPU efficiency. With dynamic batching (latency-first), the runtime will release early for small batches to hit SLOs; throughput suffers slightly. With throughput-first or fixed batching windows (say 20ms-50ms), you get better tokens/sec but p95 can jump. In your runs, 50ms batching improved tokens/sec by ~35% but increased p95 by ~80ms which breaches your 300ms SLO on search route.
[00:03:20] Samir Patel: So if we cap batch window at 20ms we hit SLOs but only get a 15% tokens/sec gain?
[00:03:25] Priya Nair: That's what we observed. The sweet spot for your traffic shape was 15-25ms. We can tune per-route.
[00:03:30] Maya Lopez: Per-route tuning is fine, but operational complexity increases. How manageable is that with Redwood Console?
[00:03:36] Alex Chen: Good question - Console supports per-route configs and rollout policies; you can A/B and canary the batch settings. Priya can set defaults and you can lock in.
[00:03:43] Priya Nair: Also autoscaling interacts: with dedicated you can set minimum pool size so burst capacity is available and batch windows can be lower.
[00:03:50] Jordan Reeves: About cache TTLs - what did you assume? We have short lived sessions, 30s to 5m.
[00:03:55] Priya Nair: For the QnA route we set TTL to 12 hours for shared corp prefix, for session-specific KV we used 2 minutes. Shorter TTL reduces cache hit ratio; if your sessions are short the savings shrink.
[00:04:05] Samir Patel: I'm slightly worried about the hosted fallback - if dedicated is down, does Redwood route to hosted and preserve same quant/model?
[00:04:11] Alex Chen: We do automated fallback to a compatible model variant, but you should expect small latency differences. We'll document exact model mappings in the runbook.
[00:04:18] Maya Lopez: About our cost spreadsheet - we saw a line item for "idle amortized GPU". Can you explain how that changes with commitment?
[00:04:24] Priya Nair: Sure. If you commit to reserved capacity, the amortized cost per token drops because the monthly GPU cost is divided across more tokens. If your effective utilization increases from 30% to 70% with batch + cache, tokens/$ improves dramatically. The sheet has a sensitivity table.
[00:04:37] Jordan Reeves: Any recommended quant profiles? You said int8 worked ok, but we have some long-form routes.
[00:04:42] Priya Nair: We recommended three profiles: full fp16 for longform, int8 high-precision for short responses, and int8 aggressive for low-criticality broadcast routes. We'll attach sample config names.
[00:04:52] Samir Patel: Can we see an example of the per-route config in console?
[00:04:55] Priya Nair: I'll export a snippet with the batching window, prefered quant profile, and cache TTL per route.
[00:04:59] Alex Chen: Ok, logistically - Samir, can your team run the 30-minute peak throughput test we outlined? We'll provide a load script and exact seed.
[00:05:06] Samir Patel: Yes, we can run it. Jordan will help with infra.
[00:05:09] Jordan Reeves: Yep. We'll need the s3 logs and an agent for collection.
[00:05:12] Priya Nair: We'll also instrument token-level billing so you can see tokens/sec/$.
[00:05:16] Maya Lopez: A few quick clarifying Qs: do we need to change our data residency for cache?
[00:05:20] Priya Nair: For prefix cache in VPC it stays in your VPC. For hosted, cache is in Redwood-managed region; we can pin region for compliance.
[00:05:28] Ellen Zhang: (joins) Apologies for being late - quick summary pls?
[00:05:31] Alex Chen: Briefly - caching yields big savings where prefixes overlap; batching increases tokens/sec but can impact p95; quant gives 2-2.5x tokens/$ improvements for certain routes. We're going to run a 30-min benchmark and Redwood will share updated cost models.
[00:05:45] Ellen Zhang: Thanks. On security follow-up - I'd like KMS and audit logs evidence.
[00:05:49] Alex Chen: We'll schedule that with Jordan.
[00:05:53] Samir Patel: One more thing - what about partial responses / streaming? Some of our product uses streaming; does batching affect streaming latency?
[00:05:59] Priya Nair: Streaming and batching is a tricky interaction. If you need first-byte low latency, dynamic batching with small windows is best; fixed batching can delay first chunk. We can configure streaming to flush partial tokens faster.
[00:06:10] Maya Lopez: Great. Can you also send the golden set eval results for quant vs fp16?
[00:06:15] Priya Nair: Yes - I'll attach the eval CSV and the sample diffs.
[00:06:18] Alex Chen: Any blockers?
[00:06:20] Jordan Reeves: We need the network diagram and KMS details before approving dedicated.
[00:06:23] Alex Chen: Noted.
[00:06:25] Priya Nair: Next sync - same time next week? We can review the benchmark and update configs.
[00:06:30] Maya Lopez: Works for us.
[00:06:32] Alex Chen: OK great. Quick recap of next steps... (recap follows)
[00:06:40] Alex Chen: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with the spreadsheet and the load script.
[00:06:45] Samir Patel: Thanks.
[00:06:46] Jordan Reeves: Thanks all.
[00:06:48] Alex Chen: Bye.
